question: Should OpenClaw support a first-class agent-ID rename transaction, and if so, should it preserve explicit workspace paths while moving only owned default paths and require plugins to opt into state migration?
rationale: The current ownership mismatch is intentional; choosing path ownership rules, plugin participation, interruption recovery, and the permanent public CLI/gateway contract cannot safely be inferred from implementation details alone.

options.title: Sponsor a bounded core rename contract
options.body: Define the transaction, workspace ownership rule, plugin migration interface, rollback journal, and recovery boundary before assigning implementation work.

options.title: Defer the capability
options.body: Keep the current strict ownership boundary and decline a supported rename flow until an owner can commit to the cross-state migration contract.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a bounded core rename contract
recommendation.body: Define the transaction, workspace ownership rule, plugin migration interface, rollback journal, and recovery boundary before assigning implementation work.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available low-confidence routing candidate from adjacent per-agent architecture discussion; no code-history ownership could be confirmed in this read-only review environment.
